messages:
Maria (Support): Hey team — customer reporting intermittent 401s in the UI when they click \"Sign in\". They included a request id in the UI: `req_0xabc123`. Asking for minimal repro bundle (HAR + console) and a curl repro if possible so we can escalate.
Devon (Eng): Thanks — can you confirm browser + version and whether this is behind a company SSO or our auth flow? For HAR we need: Preserve log, disable cache, reproduce, then export 'Save all as HAR with content'.
Customer: Chrome 117 on macOS, regular Redwood login (not SSO). Happens ~1/10 tries, no steps to reproduce reliably.
Maria (Support): OK — share these instructions with them. Keep it minimal so users can follow quickly. Suggest: 1) DevTools open (F12 / Option+Cmd+I). 2) Network tab -> check 'Preserve log'. 3) Click the three-dot menu -> Network -> 'Disable cache' (DevTools must stay open). 4) Reproduce the failure (click Sign in). 5) Right-click any request -> 'Save all as HAR with content'. Also capture Console tab: right-click -> Save as... or copy visible errors.
Kevin (SRE): Add a note for brave/safari quirks: Brave shields can modify requests — ask them to test with shields off. Safari: use Develop -> Show Web Inspector -> Network -> Save as HAR (older Safari may need 'Export HAR' via a plugin).
Devon (Eng): Include how to get the curl repro from the failing request: right-click the failing request in Network -> Copy -> 'Copy as cURL'. Remind them to redact auth tokens before pasting here. Example we ask them to run locally to confirm:
```
# run in terminal to replicate headers (redact bearer)
curl 'https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/sessions' \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"email":"you@example.com","flow":"ui"}' \
  -v
```
Maria (Support): Checklist to request from customer (copy this in the ticket):
- HAR file ("Save all as HAR with content")
- Console log snippet (errors/warnings, timestamps)
- The copied cURL for the failing request (with tokens redacted)
- Exact browser & version, OS, and whether extensions are enabled (Brave shields, adblockers)
- The UI request id they saw (`req_0xabc123`) and the local timestamp when it happened
Devon (Eng): Also useful: if they can repro, have them open the failing request -> Headers tab -> copy Response headers (especially `x-request-id`, `x-replay-id`, `x-auth-status`) and paste them here. If they can’t repro, HAR + console still helps us see earlier redirects/cookies.
Customer: Ok I can try. Where do I upload the HAR?
Maria (Support): You can attach directly to this support ticket, or if the file is large use our secure upload link: https://uploads.redwood-inference.com/<ticket-id> — we'll post a pre-signed URL if needed. Please include the `req_0xabc123` and local timestamp in the upload notes.
SupportBot: Reminder: When a HAR is uploaded, internal ticket will automatically tag Eng oncall and attach the file to the ticket (do not include any PII).
Kevin (SRE): One more tip: have them toggle to incognito with extensions off to rule out extension interference. If using corporate network, ask them to retry from home or mobile hotspot to rule out middleboxes.
Maria (Support): Great — once they upload, please ping @Devon and @Kevin here with the support ticket number. I'll add the steps to the ticket so the customer can follow easily. :thumbsup:
Devon (Eng): If we get the HAR and cURL, I'll try to reproduce and inc to the runtime logs for that `x-request-id`/`req_0xabc123`.
Maria (Support): Thanks all — sending instructions to the customer now.
